decision: Keep two implementation graphs
before: The CLI composes app-local mechanisms; the daemon package mainly offers contracts and policy.
after: The package gains mechanisms and DaemonClient; the shipped dispatcher still imports the CLI copies. The 38-file freeze protects the prepared head, excludes three host-routing files, normalizes CRLF, and does not compare the two implementations.
reason: Stated: separate mechanism ownership from host invocation review (PR body). Portable hashing is specified by commit subjects; no separate reason for this exact digest scheme was found.

decision: Give mechanisms a package home
before: Mechanisms and an output codec live under the CLI.
after: Ten directories own client, process, registry, transport, worker, execution, delivery, resources, diagnostics and lifecycle. The package has no internal production dependency. The spool gets a local record codec; protocol, policy defaults, navigation algorithms and pre-existing session/delivery boundaries are retained.
reason: Stated: one enforced daemon boundary, with no knowledge of symbols or CLI implementation (architecture plan).

decision: Make executable entries real
before: The shipped process and worker resolve CLI entry files.
after: The package exports root, process-entry and worker-entry; the last two execute for side effects, with no named entry API. Package launchers/workers resolve their own relative artifacts and load the supplied executor module. The CLI path still resolves its own entries.
reason: Stated: executable entries belong to package extraction; commits require exact entry exports.

decision: Let the host supply product knowledge and policy
before: The CLI selects argv/workspace and constructs mechanisms.
after: The host supplies state directory, version, enabled flag, executor factory/module URL and readiness command/argv. Each execute supplies workspace, classified command, argv, cwd and telemetry. Policy is optional and otherwise comes from currentSystem; a supplied policy changes the client’s values.
reason: Stated: syntax and product work stay in the host. Unexplained: the specific optional-policy exposure/default choice is implemented but has no separate comparative reason in the inspected record.

decision: Retain one loading promise
before: No public DaemonClient exists.
after: The Node-free façade starts dynamic loading at construction. Every execute/control awaits that same runtime promise, including a retained rejection. Portable declarations do not imply a browser runtime. The methods do not retry the load.
reason: Stated: host declarations must avoid Node ambient dependencies. Unexplained: construction-time loading and retention of a failed load.

decision: Retain client composition, distinguish control clocks
before: CLI dispatcher construction is per request; lifecycle composition is exposed.
after: One client runtime retains registry, startup coordinator, transports and controllers. Status uses its separate response timeout: 100 ms by default versus 250 ms for ordinary exchanges. Control overloads return action-specific reports; mechanism failures reject to the host.
reason: Stated: the policy plan separates status responsiveness from routing. Unexplained: exact retained composition and the choice to expose those control rejections through this interface.

decision: Disable execution/start without disabling observation
before: The enabled flag controls daemon use.
after: Disabled execute runs cold without registry routing; disabled start returns disabled. Status and stop remain callable. A disabled route variant is declared internally, but the four guards do not produce it: execute short-circuits first.
reason: Unexplained: no distinct reason for the disabled-control asymmetry or unused route variant was found. The behavior is visible in code and characterization.

decision: Stop at the first routing decision
before: The dispatcher owns the routing branches.
after: After the enabled check: record present → not starting → version compatible → responsive. Record reads and observations are lazy and memoized. A starting record wins over its old version; later observation is skipped. Read/observation failures select recovering.
reason: Stated: the first decision must prevent later side effects (PR body and architecture plan).

decision: Keep local attempts separate from warming
before: Local/cold/fallback execution and daemon startup are separately coordinated.
after: Absent selects cold plus independent startup; dead/incompatible select fallback plus startup; starting/recovering select cold without another trigger. Confirmed exit permits exact-process removal. Trigger errors are swallowed. Each local attempt gets a fresh executor and no-op resource sampler; local executor errors are not converted by the warm-error handler.
reason: Stated: answer ordinary commands locally while warming, without canceling or duplicating them (functional plan). Unexplained: a separate reason for the exact local factory/sampler shape was not found.

decision: Choose the warm request’s protocol source
before: The dispatcher writes record.protocolVersion into the request.
after: The new client writes the package’s DAEMON_PROTOCOL_VERSION. Endpoint, instance and token still come from the observed record; each submission receives a new request ID. This changes value authority, not an established normal wire value.
reason: Unexplained: no separate reason for choosing the constant over the stored field was found.

decision: Keep replay permission with transport
before: The existing transport error vocabulary distinguishes safe failure from uncertain/accepted work.
after: Only a DaemonTransportError marked retrySafe allows local fallback from warm submission. Uncertain or accepted failure stays warm and returns exit 1. Resource, response-capacity and other failures retain three controlled stderr outcomes.
reason: Stated: retry safety and failure output belong to the daemon client; disconnect is not permission to replay accepted work.

decision: Own capture and malformed-output disposal
before: The shipped dispatcher uses CLI result construction; its malformed-result branch does not dispose the available output.
after: The client creates a fresh policy-limited capture for a warm transfer, spilling to the OS temporary directory, and returns output with records/dispose. Noninteger exit code or missing output yields a controlled warm failure; available malformed output is disposed first, disposal failure is swallowed, and no local replay follows. Valid returned output is consumed/disposed by its caller.
reason: Stated: warm transfer cleanup and result construction belong to the client (PR body).

decision: Validate adopted coordinates at constructor entry
before: The executable entry checks derived keys/endpoint; WorkspaceDaemon accepts separate identity scalars.
after: DaemonProcessCoordinator takes the coordinate object and synchronously rejects mismatched root/keys/endpoint before reading its policy option. It listens/publishes the adopted endpoint. Direct construction now carries the validation contract; entry identity validation already existed. Worker policy parsing before new Worker also already existed at this PR’s base.
reason: Unexplained: commits specify validated adoption, but no comparative reason for this exact constructor boundary or the additional root comparison was found.

decision: Narrow composition ports, retain lifecycle owners
before: WorkspaceDaemon binds execution, delivery, worker, resource and lifetime collaborators.
after: The renamed coordinator requires a daemon clock, calls a serving-only server port and accepts workspaceExists instead of a generic fs dependency. Six cyclic callbacks remain inert during construction and delegate when invoked. Existing execution/delivery waits and owners are retained.
reason: Stated: separate process coordination from product concerns. Unexplained: the precise port and callback construction choices have no separate recorded reason.

decision: Make ownership equality authoritative
before: Some ownership operations accept a matching instance ID alone; exact-owner operations compare full observations.
after: Named registry operations use one predicate. Identity and instance are always required; credentials, kind, PID and exact snapshot fields refine the expectation. A readable lock with the same instance but a conflicting identity now fails isStartupOwner and refreshStartupOwner. Adoption/removal rechecks exact owners. These edits reach the live CLI before freezing.
reason: Stated: one owner for lock equality (architecture plan). Unexplained: no separate reconciliation of the tightened outcomes with preservation intent was found.

decision: Preserve request-specific authentication order
before: The dispatcher already distinguishes identity/termination from execution-family requests.
after: Identify/terminate/kill check instance+token on their early branches. Other requests check protocol+instance first; execute, status-of-execution, fetch and ACK also check token before state access. Ping and stop remain on protocol+instance only. New direct harness tests characterize these differences.
reason: Unexplained: no specific rationale for the inherited asymmetry/order was found. Characterization states the behavior; it does not explain why that boundary was chosen.

decision: Own wall and elapsed clocks
before: Daemon timing includes telemetry Clock, optional now callbacks and scattered sources.
after: DaemonClock supplies wall time for deadlines/timestamps and monotonic time for queue/worker durations. The standalone queue default changes to monotonic. Injected clock ownership does not change the operating policy or establish a new process boundary.
reason: Stated: daemon owns wall and monotonic clocks; telemetry is a leaf (architecture plan).

decision: Keep the old idle events
before: Idle timing starts at construction and resets when navigation is accepted.
after: Those events remain. Readiness and completion do not reset the deadline; completion may immediately trigger shutdown once the queue becomes idle after the deadline. The 30-minute default stays. Readiness-armed and completion-based intervals are added as deferred work.
reason: Stated: preserve extraction behavior and defer these lifetime changes (PR body and follow-up plan).

decision: Move tests with mechanisms
before: 37 direct mechanism test files live with the CLI; some fixtures import its executor.
after: Those suites move to package owners, with generic executors and package-local canonical-path, output and policy helpers. CLI-facing/e2e tests remain on the compatibility path. Their success cannot by itself establish active use of DaemonClient or pairwise equivalence.
reason: Stated: tests reaching daemon internals must move or use the public surface; generic fixtures keep the package independent of the CLI.

decision: Re-anchor the version rejection witness
before: A worker starts the real CLI executor with a wrong version and expects initialization failure.
after: That integrated case disappears. A direct createDaemonExecutor wrong-version rejection test is added in the CLI. Generic missing-module/export worker failures remain, but they exercise different stimuli.
reason: Stated: isolate package fixtures. Unexplained: no equivalence argument or distinct reason for losing the worker→CLI version-classification path was found.

decision: Remove seven timing expectations from readiness
before: The CLI worker readiness case checks three startup and four execution durations.
after: Generic readiness retains fileCount, readiness, result exit code and output bytes. The three startupDurations and four durations fields are removed from that case. No claim is made that all timing coverage disappears.
reason: Unexplained: no reason for these precise assertion removals was found.

decision: Replace entry witnesses at a different boundary
before: The deleted CLI entry file checks mocked configuration/observer wiring, including a 257 MiB worker-policy handoff, and a source import restriction.
after: New built package process/worker tests observe real entry resolution, generic executor behavior and failure cleanup; the launcher test mocks spawn. The inspected new built-entry cases do not recreate the exact 257 MiB mocked entry assertion. Real execution and exact policy handoff are distinct propositions.
reason: Stated: package entries must be executable. Unexplained: no argument that the new witnesses replace each deleted entry assertion was found.

decision: State what the new guards and client tests observe
before: The base clock test has no raw-source guard; public-client tests are new.
after: The head’s raw-clock guard scans only lifecycle siblings, despite its broad title. Public tests cover declaration shape, exact exports and disabled cold execution; warm route/control tests instantiate the internal runtime and supply mocked outcomes. Boundary checks are useful but do not establish full CLI parity.
reason: Stated: enforce package/portable declaration boundaries. Unexplained: the one-directory clock-scan scope has no located reason.

decision: Retire temporary testing access on its recorded condition
before: policy-testing exposes a temporary override factory, guarded by lint/meta-tests.
after: The export and special lint cases retire; local helpers replace imports, and exact root/process/worker export checks remain. The pinned migration plan says to remove the subpath after app-owned mechanism tests move package-local. That is recorded context, even though the patch does not edit that paragraph.
reason: Stated: the plan gives the retirement condition. Unexplained: that condition does not individually justify every removed assertion.

decision: Give forced-exit cleanup a platform-specific observer
before: The deleted mocked entry witness does not execute platform-specific termination.
after: The new built-process test expects Windows to retain a ready record without a termination diagnostic until a surviving observer removes it. Other platforms expect child cleanup and one diagnostic. Both end without the record/owner. This is a source assertion, not a Windows run by this experiment.
reason: Unexplained: the final commit specifies the Windows expectation but supplies no explanatory body.

decision: Serialize package test files; provide their loader
before: The daemon package has no local Vitest scheduling override and its test helpers are not yet relocated.
after: The new config sets fileParallelism:false. tsx ^4.21.0 and its lockfile importer support TypeScript helper processes; local test policy helpers remove the public testing subpath dependency.
reason: Unexplained: no specific reason for serialization, that loader/version range, or source-running helpers over built helpers was found. The helper call sites show use, not motive.
